### Observed differences

- In the later window, activities A21–A24 drop from about 83 in 100 traces to about 28 in 100, while A25–A28 rise from about 18 in 100 to about 73 in 100. [OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, OCC008, OCC009, OCC010, OCC011]
- A04 drops from about 55 in 100 traces to about 16 in 100; A02 and A08 increase slightly, from about 5% to 14% and 4% to 12% respectively. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003]
- A31’s outgoing behaviour shifts: before, about 53% of its transitions went to A04 and 45% to A19; after, about 84% go to A19 and only 6% to A04. [DIR004]
- A20’s outgoing behaviour shifts: before, about 83% went to A24 and 18% to A28; after, about 72% go to A28 and 27% to A24. [DIR003]
- A04’s main successor A19 drops from about 87% of A04 transitions to about 32%, with new successors such as A16, A35, A31 and A37 appearing. [DIR001]
- A19 and A20 co-occur with A21–A24 in about 83% of traces before but only about 28% after; their co-occurrence with A25–A28 rises from about 18% to about 73%, with A19/A20 before A25–A28 in about 71% of traces. [REL013, REL014, REL015, REL016, REL017, REL018, REL019, REL020, REL021, REL022, REL023, REL024, REL025, REL026, REL027, REL028]
- A31 is before A21–A24 in about 80% of traces before, but after it is before A25–A28 in about 72% of traces, while co-occurrence with A21–A24 drops to about 28%. [REL036, REL044, REL051, REL057, REL062, REL066, REL069, REL071]
- Lag distances confirm the shift: A31–A19 at lag 1 rises from about 45% to 84%, A31–A20 at lag 2 from about 44% to 81%, and A31–A28 at lag 3 from about 44% to 82%. [LAG007, LAG008, LAG010]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports a structural change in which the later process largely skips A04 and replaces the A21–A24 block with A25–A28, with A31 and A20 routing directly to the new block. The participation swap, the successor changes for A31 and A20, and the relational and lag evidence all point in the same direction: A31 and A19/A20 now lead to A25–A28 instead of to A04 and A21–A24. [OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, OCC008, OCC009, OCC010, OCC011, DIR003, DIR004, REL017, REL018, REL019, REL020, REL025, REL026, REL027, REL028, REL062, REL066, REL069, REL071, LAG007, LAG008, LAG010]

A competing explanation is that the windows simply contain different case mixes, and the variant-frequency differences alone could produce some of the participation changes. However, the direct successor and order changes are not explained by sampling alone. A limitation is that A04-related evidence in the later window rests on only about 31 traces, and some lag details on even fewer, so the exact new position of A04 is less certain. [OCC002, DIR001, LAG001, LAG002]
